pixel_convention: x right, y down, full-resolution pixels
view: Top-down (bird's-eye) camera looking straight down at a paved promenade beside water; motion is on the ground plane, which faces the camera (2D).

camera.evidence: phase correlation of the pavement region (y 0-450, x 450-1900) vs frame 0: shift 0.00 px in every frame; frame differences only at the animal (plus faint grass sway at x<120, y~600)
camera.perspective: near-orthographic top view; pavement groove spacing is uniform (144.7 px) across the frame, so one px scale holds on the ground plane. Raised parts (lounger backrests) appear slightly flared.

moving_objects.name: animal

moving_objects.reference_point: body_cx, body_cy = centroid of the body mask with the thin tail removed (proxy for the rig root/pelvis-body centre, seen from above). full_cx/full_cy include the tail.
moving_objects.direction: +x (rightwards), essentially straight: net dx = +266.4 px, dy = -3.5 px over frames 0-49

pixel_step_per_frame.note: the std comes from the gait (body centroid shifts with leg/head pose); a linear fit of body_cx vs frame gives 5.47 px/frame with a negligible quadratic term (-0.0005 px/frame^2), i.e. constant walking speed
